title: Lesson 19 - Lead to Opportunity: Conversion Mechanics, Sales Processes, and Path
description: Given a set of requirements, construct an end-to-end sales process within Salesforce that supports the business from Lead to Opportunity to Quote to Close.

questions.question: A rep converts a Lead whose record type is Enterprise. The rep's profile default Account record type is Standard. What record type does the new Account get?
options: Standard, the new owner's profile default
The org default Account record type regardless of profile
None; accounts created by conversion have no record type
questions.explanation: Conversion assigns the new owner's profile default record type rather than the Lead's type, which is why orgs that need inheritance build an explicit mapping.

questions.question: The Standard and Enterprise teams must use different stage sets on the same Opportunity object. What do you configure?
options: Two Opportunity record types, each assigned a different sales process
Two page layouts on one record type
A validation rule that hides stages per team
questions.explanation: A sales process defines which global Stage values a record type may use, so two record types each pointed at their own process is the supported pattern.

questions.question: A previously converted Lead shows its Phone field as read-only. Why?
options: The lead was merged into a duplicate
Field-level security was changed during conversion
Converting a lead places the converted lead record in a read-only state that stays linked to the new account, contact, and opportunity
The lead record type removed edit access
questions.explanation: Conversion is permanent and makes the Salesforce-managed lead fields read-only while keeping the link to the created records; it is not a security or record type effect.
